answer: A new identity must plant a non-transferable nectar bond in a public garden maintained by already-established operators. Admission then depends on surviving a series of zephyr audits: brief, randomly timed challenges issued by three non-adjacent garden jurors who each assign unique unpaid work and countersign only original answers. If two applicants share an operator key, their nectar records collide and both bonds are slashed. Until six clean zephyr rounds are signed, rewards stay locked, so a farm cannot mint many full shares from one wallet.
